name: Airtable
summary: This guide covers setting up OAuth2 authentication with Airtable by registering your own OAuth app via the Airtable Developer/Builder Hub. You will use the official Airtable OAuth integration flow to obtain the necessary credentials (Client ID, Client Secret), register a redirect URL (as required by your platform, such as Composio), set the correct scopes, and connect your account for token-based access.
decision: To set up OAuth with Airtable, register a new OAuth integration in the Airtable Developer (or Builder) Hub, provide the correct redirect URI for your integration platform, copy the Client ID and Client Secret, add and save the recommended scopes, and authorize your account via the consent screen. Complete the remaining steps in your integration platform (e.g., Composio dashboard), ensuring the redirect URI matches exactly. If you do not already have OAuth credentials, you must use this path.

prerequisites.title: Create an Airtable Account
prerequisites.body: You need an active Airtable account with access to the necessary bases or data.

prerequisites.title: Access to Airtable Developer Hub
prerequisites.body: You must be able to access the Airtable Developer or Builder Hub to register a new OAuth integration.
prerequisites.note: Also called Builder Hub in some documentation.

steps.title: Navigate to Airtable Developer/Builder Hub
steps.body: Go to https://airtable.com/developers/web/api or https://airtable.com/create/oauth to begin the OAuth integration registration process.
steps.note: URLs are provided in both Composio and Amazon Quick guides.

steps.title: Register New OAuth Integration
steps.body: In the Developer/Builder Hub, select 'OAuth integrations' and then '+ New OAuth Integration' (or 'Register new OAuth integration'). Enter a name and optional description/website for the app.

steps.title: Configure the Redirect URI
steps.body: Paste the integration platform's required redirect URL into the 'OAuth redirect URLs' field. For Composio, use: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback (no trailing slash, protocol must be https).
steps.note: Composio provides the required URL. Amazon Quick requires its own URL.

steps.title: Generate Client ID and Client Secret
steps.body: After registering your integration, Airtable will provide a Client ID. Use the 'Generate client secret' option to obtain the Client Secret.

steps.title: Set OAuth Scopes
steps.body: In the app configuration, add scopes according to your requirements. Common recommended scopes are: data.records:read, data.records:write, schema.bases:read. Additional scopes can be added (e.g., data.recordComments:read/write, schema.bases:write, user.email:read) if needed.
steps.note: Composio and Amazon Quick both list common scopes.

steps.title: Save Changes and Record Credentials
steps.body: Record your OAuth Client ID and Client Secret. Save the integration in Airtable.

steps.title: Configure the Integration Platform
steps.body: Open your integration platform (e.g., Composio dashboard), select Airtable, choose OAuth2 authentication, and paste the Client ID, Client Secret, and configure scopes to match your Airtable app.

steps.title: Authorize Connection
steps.body: Initiate the OAuth flow by clicking 'Connect Account' (or equivalent). In the authorization dialog, log in to your Airtable account, review and accept the requested permissions, select bases/workspaces, and approve the connection.

steps.title: Verify Connection and Complete Setup
steps.body: Ensure your integration platform confirms successful connection, and use the provided Auth Config ID (Composio) or corresponding identifier for further API use.

blockers.title: Lack of Developer Hub/Builder Hub Access
blockers.body: You cannot complete the OAuth registration and obtain required credentials without access to the correct Airtable interface.

blockers.title: Redirect URI Mismatch
blockers.body: The redirect URI entered in Airtable must match the one used by your integration platform exactly, or OAuth authorization will fail.

human_actions.title: Register an OAuth application in Airtable
human_actions.body: Log in to Airtable and manually register the OAuth app, entering redirect URI and scopes.

human_actions.title: Copy and paste credentials
human_actions.body: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret and securely enter them into your integration platform’s configuration.

human_actions.title: Initiate and complete the OAuth consent flow
human_actions.body: Manually approve access in the consent dialog during authorization, selecting bases/workspaces as needed.
